column1: # The woman's parts: one row per part of data/anatomy_f, built by build_f.py from the Human Reference Atlas female set (v1.10, file u)
# and its female pelvis (v1.3, file p). Columns (tab-separated):
#   id       the part's id (the app shows it with the prefix vhf_); the same id as the man's part where the structure is the same
#   name     shown on screen; {Side} is Left or Right, {n} the source node's own name in words (rows with flag each)
#   system   one of the app's systems (integumentary skeletal muscular nervous cardiovascular respiratory digestive urinary
#   side     - (none), L or R (only meshes on that side, by position), LR (one part per side: id_l and id_r)
#   match    regular expression on the node's path (ancestor names and its own, joined by /, VH_F_ removed); a subtree is chosen
#   exclude  regular expression; matching nodes are left out (- for none)
#   file     u (united female v1.10) or p (pelvis female v1.3)
#   tris     triangle target after reduction (per side for LR; L/R targets as a/b)
#   src      where the shape comes from: vhf (her sections), vhf_edited (her sections, adjusted by the atlas makers), vhf_atlas
#            (her sections, modelled with the guidance of atlases), modelled (fitted to her body, not traced), sculpted (a
#            sculpted reference model placed in her body), allen (another woman's brain, Allen atlas, mirrored and resized)
#   card     the card (node id in data/nodes) that explains it
#   parent   - or the part this one is a detail of (drawn only in that organ's cut-open view)
#   flags    - or a comma list: whole (the part has detail parts), each (one part per matched node)
# Sides are set from position, never from the source's names (some of which are wrong: the Allen "_L" structures and the
# "right" round ligament lie on her right and left respectively). build_f.py logs every name that disagrees with its position.
